SNMP v2c asks for a community instead of a user and a password. Changing an interface or the name, contact and location of the system needs a community that may write; there is no rollback like Safe Mode.

The user and password are those of an SNMPv3 user; with no password the agent is asked without authentication. In RouterOS the user is the name of an /snmp community, the passwords its authentication-password and encryption-password. NetworkHelm is a client for routers: one menu tree, windows in a single workspace, tables that update live, item dialogs with tabs, Safe Mode, a terminal and a file browser. It works with MikroTik RouterOS 7 and 6, OpenWrt, OPNsense, pfSense, VyOS, Keenetic and Netcraze, Linux hosts over SSH, and works with devices over SNMP and UPnP. One Kotlin codebase builds for Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS and the browser. The app sends nothing to its developer: no account, no analytics, no crash reports.
